post.title: Tiny World Builder
post.hook: A browser voxel world editor that grew into flight combat and multiplayer.
post.summary: A self-contained 3D voxel world editor in the browser for building, sculpting, flying through and sharing tiny worlds. It reached 651 commits in about six weeks and picked up multiplayer, flight combat and an on-chain worlds mode.
post.writeup:
## What it is
Tiny World Builder is a 3D voxel world editor that runs in the browser. You place terrain, houses, trees, crops and animals, sculpt the ground, switch camera modes, fly through the result and share it.

## Why it exists
The goal is a toy-like diorama where the 3D scene is the hero and the UI floats above it as frosted glass. The design doc describes a warm parchment world with one blue accent.

## How it works
The app is a single script of roughly 29k lines of vanilla JS, split later into engine modules. `world[x][z]` holds intent, `cellMeshes` holds the rendered Three.js groups, and `setCell(x, z, opts)` is the single mutation entry point. It re-renders neighbors so roads join, fences connect and houses form L, T and square buildings.

Around that core sit several layers:
- Mesh Terrain sculptor with flat-topped voxels
- Seeded vehicle road demos with live traffic blockers
- PartyKit shared building with remote cursors
- Stunt-plane combat plans: guns, HUD, guided missiles
- A worlds mode where players buy land with USDC
- i18n in English, French, Spanish and Chinese

## Results
The repo has 651 commits from 7 authors between 2026-05-10 and 2026-06-19. The busiest week was 2026-06-01 with 183 commits. An advisor pass produced 6 plans, all marked DONE. A review of recent commits found 20 issues: 3 high, 3 medium and 14 low.

## Open questions
Plan 005 shipped 3 of 4 tests because mock.module() needs a flag the test script lacks. The latest commit adds living-lobby plans and an onboarding audit, so the first-run experience is still being shaped.
